incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: model-catalog service — high severity
incident-bot: Rule: catalog.default-revision-change - detected default model revision change to `rev-2026-03-bad` which is not compatible with tokenizer v2
pagerduty: Incident PD123456 created — severity: P1 — automatic escalation
pagerduty: Paging oncall Alex (oncall)
Alex (oncall): ack
Alex (oncall): I see errors in the runtime logs for tokenization failures and 502s to the serving fleet. Taking ownership.
Carlos (support): Multiple customers reported garbled embeddings and tokenization errors in embeddings endpoint. Ticket counts: 7 high-priority orgs so far.
Raj (eng-runtime): Logs show model variant `rev-2026-03-bad` was promoted to default by a batch job at 10:41Z. It's missing the tokenizer map `v2->v1-fallback` and default token config looks like:
```
model_defaults:
  sampling: top_p=0.95
  tokenizer: "v2"
  max_seq: 2048
```
Those defaults break older tokenizers used by embeddings pipeline.
Alex (oncall): Can we pin back the previous default quickly? What's the rollback command?
Raj (eng-runtime): Use the catalog CLI to set default revision:
```
redwood catalog set-default --model-name=open-embed --revision=rev-2026-02-stable --reason="rollback bad default"
```
I'll run it in a minute. Mei, can you standby for cluster-level fallout?
Mei (eng-sre): Standing by. If traffic spikes we'll throttle and fold to fallback model group. Prepare canary routing to rev-2026-02-stable.
Priya (product): Heads-up — billing customers on Dedicated may see latency. Need short customer message. Carlos, can you assemble a one-liner for status page?
Carlos (support): Draft: "We detected a model configuration change causing tokenization errors for some embedding requests. We are rolling back the catalog default and expect full recovery within 10 minutes. If you continue to see issues, contact support." Thoughts?
Priya (product): Good. Add "no data exfiltration" and estimated impact window 10-30m.
Raj (eng-runtime): Executing rollback now.
```
# run as redwood-deploy
redwood catalog set-default --model-name=open-embed --revision=rev-2026-02-stable --reason="auto-rollback for tokenizer mismatch"
```
pagerduty: PD123456 acknowledged by Alex (oncall)
Alex (oncall): rollback command returned success, catalog change propagated to control plane. Rolling out routing change to serve stable revision.
Mei (eng-sre): Observability: errors dropping, tokenization errors rate down from 18% -> 1.2% in last 3m. Thundering herd mitigated by autoscale, no node OOMs.
Raj (eng-runtime): Confirmed model servers are now serving rev-2026-02-stable. KV-cache warmup in progress; transient higher latencies expected.
Carlos (support): Posted to status page and notified affected customers. Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/PD123456
Priya (product): Great. Alex, take incident commander or pass to Mei for postmortem?
Alex (oncall): I'll hand off to Mei for full postmortem. I'll stay on for 15m then sign off.
Mei (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem. Action items:
- investigate why the batch job promoted a revision without tokenizer validation
- add pre-promotion validation step in catalog CI
- add automated rollback policy if tokenizer mismatch detected
- customer outreach follow-up
Alex (oncall): Adding runbook note: ensure pager config has explicit owner for catalog changes.
